questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.topic: Why a restoration's settlement held
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a restoration settlement endured
questions.stem: A restored monarchy keeps power after a revolution; which factor best explains why its settlement held?

options.text: Broad elites accepted the settlement and foreign powers guaranteed it
The restored king ruled by decree alone without support
The revolutionaries all died in battle
No taxes were collected after restoration

questions.explanation: Elite acceptance plus foreign guarantee sustained the settlement; decree-alone reading misses support.
questions.hint: Who must accept a settlement for it to last?

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.topic: What an amendment clause adds to a charter
questions.learningObjective: Identify what an amendment clause adds to a charter
questions.stem: A charter gains an amendment clause; explain what that clause adds to the original text.

answer.exemplar: The amendment clause adds a lawful procedure for changing the charter, making future revisions possible without breaking the whole document.

questions.explanation: An amendment clause supplies a lawful revision procedure without rupturing the charter.
questions.hint: It is a mechanism for change, not change itself.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.topic: A revolution's effect on a neighbouring state
questions.learningObjective: Assess a revolution's effect on a neighbour

stimulus.body: A neighbouring state sees refugees arrive and ideas spread. Its government tightens censorship. Trade continues across the border.

questions.stem: What effect did the revolution most likely have on the neighbour?

options.text: The neighbour invaded immediately to restore the old regime
options.misconception: assumes military response not in the memo

options.text: The neighbour abolished all taxes in solidarity
The neighbour restricted expression while trade continued
The neighbour welcomed the revolution openly

questions.explanation: Censorship tightened while trade continued; invasion and solidarity readings add unsupported claims.
questions.hint: Read both the restriction and the continuity.

provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.topic: Why a reform's route provoked resistance
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a reform's chosen route provoked resistance

stimulus.body: A reform is imposed from above by decree. Local elites are bypassed. Petitions protest the lack of consultation.

questions.stem: Why did the reform's route provoke resistance?

options.text: Because the reform's content was too generous
Because it lowered taxes sharply
options.misconception: assumes a fiscal motive not stated

options.text: Because foreign troops enforced it
Because it bypassed local elites and consultation

questions.explanation: Bypassing elites and consultation provoked resistance; generosity reading confuses route with content.
questions.hint: Focus on the route, not the content.
